clue.text: Teacher to object to TV quiz

parts.note: a master is a schoolteacher
to mind something is to object to it

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher complains about a television quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastermind is a long-running BBC television quiz show with a famous black chair.

clue.text: Cry, being fat

definitions.meaning: the fat layer of a whale or seal

explanation.surface: Someone weeps because they feel overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: To blubber is to sob noisily; as a noun it is the insulating fat of sea mammals.

clue.text: Beat up around London college

indicators.note: around means the word up is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: Someone beats up a person near a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat up' looks like one phrase, but 'Beat' alone is the definition; 'around' then works on 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the regular beat of the heart felt at the wrist.

clue.text: Tell stories about fine existence

indicators.note: about means the fib word goes around the letter for fine

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: Someone spins tales about having a fine existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Life and existence are synonyms for being alive.

clue.text: Prison entrance opened by skill, taking minutes

indicators.note: opened by means the entrance word is split apart with other letters put in

parts.note: a door is an entrance

indicators.note: taking means the skill word takes on the next letter after it

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: A prison gate is skilfully opened in a matter of minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor is a well-known prison on the moors of Devon, in south-west England.

clue.text: Name tag is wrong, for example, if back to front

parts.note: bad means wrong

indicators.note: back to front means the abbreviation for example is written in reverse

explanation.surface: A name tag is printed wrongly when worn back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is a small pinned label, often bearing the wearer's name.

clue.text: Authority remains silent?

definitions.meaning: the power to decide, as in 'on whose word?'
the question mark flags the joke

explanation.surface: A person in power keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the entry as SAYS plus O: one who says nothing remains silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Say-so is the right to give permission, as in 'only on my word'.

clue.text: Check in earlier for ship

indicators.note: in means the check abbreviation is placed inside the word for earlier

parts.note: sooner means earlier
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Passengers are told to check in early for a sailing.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts.

clue.text: One doctor on large wing, say

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the earlier pieces follow the one for large

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor attends to a large bird wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is an example of a limb, as an arm or leg is; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Democrat, meeting a revolutionary, took a risk

parts.note: a red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician risked meeting a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: To dare is to venture something risky; the past tense matches 'took'.

clue.text: Small bank perhaps is inadequate

parts.note: a bank is an example of a lender of money

explanation.surface: A small bank is perhaps not up to the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means meagre or scant, as in slender means or a slender chance.

clue.text: Prepare elderly teacher for ultimate conflict

parts.note: to arm is to prepare for battle
aged means elderly
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An old schoolmaster gets ready for a final showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical last battle between good and evil at the end of the world.

clue.text: Blame for upsetting woman

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters of blame are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone points the finger at a woman for causing distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Mabel is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Pompous fellow who may burst his buttons?

definitions.text: Pompous fellow who may burst his buttons?

parts.words: Pompous fellow who may burst his buttons?
parts.note: a self-important man is pictured as so puffed up that his packed shirt front strains at the buttons

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a pompous, stuffy person, and the literal image is an overfilled garment.

clue.text: Place of exile: some feel bad

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being banished makes some people feel miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was exiled to this Mediterranean island in 1814.

clue.text: Cannon needs a lot of extra preservative

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word for extra is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: more means extra
tar is used to preserve wood and rope

explanation.surface: A gun needs plenty of extra protective coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short artillery piece firing shells at a high angle.

clue.text: An unfair practice, but relatively helpful

definitions.meaning: favouritism in giving jobs or advantages
helpful to one's relatives, a cryptic reading of 'relatively'

explanation.surface: Something unfair can still be comparatively useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' seems to mean 'comparatively' but here means 'to relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouring family members, for example in appointments.

clue.text: Determined to swear, being cussed?

definitions.meaning: minded to say the swear word 'bloody', a cryptic reading
obstinate and contrary; the question mark plays on cuss meaning swear

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to curse is being stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' is a mild British swear word, so 'minded' to say it is 'determined to swear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloody-minded means deliberately obstructive, which is what cussed means.

clue.text: Drew up, carrying one old eccentric

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the letter for one inside it
up in a down clue means the word drew is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone drew up a document involving one old oddball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DREW into WERD; 'carrying' puts I inside to give WEIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an odd, eccentric person, a colloquial noun.

clue.text: Keep bringing pints perhaps round for spectator

indicators.note: round means the drink word goes round the word for keep

parts.note: pints are typically pints of beer
to hold is to keep

explanation.surface: Someone keeps bringing a round of pints for an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like a round of drinks, but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A beholder is one who looks on, as in 'beauty is in the eye of the beholder'.

clue.text: Wait, receiving bridge partners nearby

indicators.note: receiving means the word for wait takes the partners into its middle

parts.note: to bide is to wait
East and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Bridge partners sitting close by are told to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside means at the side of, close to; used adverbially it can mean nearby.

clue.text: Eastern entertainer disguising his age

indicators.note: disguising means the letters of the following words are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A performer hides how old he is.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese hostess trained in music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Brought into the world inhaling oxygen and another element

indicators.note: inhaling means the birth word takes the oxygen symbol inside it, as lungs take in air

parts.note: born means brought into the world
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A newborn takes its first breath of oxygen and other gases.
explanation.definitionFit: Boron is a chemical element, symbol B; 'another' follows the oxygen in the clue.

clue.text: In this place hours before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone arrived at this spot hours earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Here is the adverb for at or in this location.
